title: Κολοιὸς καὶ κόρακες
part: The Jackdaw and the Ravens (Chambry 161 · Perry 123)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 161 (= Perry 123). Text as printed. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Κολοιὸς τῷ μεγέθει τῶν ἄλλων κολοιῶν διαφέρων, ὑπερφρονήσας τοὺς ὁμοφύλους, παρεγένετο πρὸς τοὺς κόρακας καὶ τούτοις ἠξίου συνδιαιτᾶσθαι.
sentences.tr: Koloios tōi megethei tōn allōn koloiōn diapherōn, hyperphronēsas tous homophylous, paregeneto pros tous korakas kai toutois ēxiou syndiaitasthai.
sentences.l: A jackdaw, surpassing the other jackdaws in size, having looked down on his own kind, came to the ravens and thought fit to share his life with them.
sentences.i: A jackdaw who outdid the other jackdaws in size looked down on his own kind, went off to the ravens, and claimed the right to live among them.
sentences.n: διαφέρω takes the genitive of what is surpassed and the dative of the respect — 'differing from the other jackdaws in size', which in practice is being bigger than they. ἠξίου, imperfect of ἀξιόω, is 'thought it fitting, claimed as his due': the verb already carries the bird's opinion of himself. συνδιαιτᾶσθαι takes the dative of the company kept, and δίαιτα, the manner of living, is the word this fable turns on; it comes back in the jackdaw fables that follow.

sentences.t: Οἱ δὲ ἀμφιγνοοῦντες αὐτοῦ τό τε εἶδος καὶ τὴν φωνὴν παίοντες αὐτὸν ἐξέβαλον.
sentences.tr: Hoi de amphignoountes autou to te eidos kai tēn phōnēn paiontes auton exebalon.
sentences.l: But they, being in doubt about both his look and his voice, beating him drove him out.
sentences.i: But they could place neither his look nor his voice, and beat him out.
sentences.n: ἀμφιγνοέω is to be of two minds about a thing and so fail to place it — not that the ravens did not see him, but that they could not tell what he was. τε … καί couples the two things that gave him away, the shape he had and the sound he made.

sentences.t: Καὶ ὃς ἀπελαθεὶς ὑπ’ αὐτῶν ἧκε πάλιν πρὸς τοὺς κολοιούς.
sentences.tr: Kai hos apelatheis hyp’ autōn hēke palin pros tous koloious.
sentences.l: And he, having been driven off by them, came back again to the jackdaws.
sentences.n: καὶ ὅς is the old demonstrative use of the relative pronoun — 'and he', standing at the head of its own sentence — a shape kept in narrative long after ὅς had settled elsewhere into being a relative.

sentences.t: Οἱ δὲ ἀγανακτοῦντες ἐπὶ τῇ ὕβρει οὐ προσεδέξαντο αὐτόν.
sentences.tr: Hoi de aganaktountes epi tēi hybrei ou prosedexanto auton.
sentences.l: But they, being indignant at the insult, did not receive him.
sentences.n: ἀγανακτέω takes ἐπί and the dative of what one is indignant at. ὕβρις is the outrage of being treated as beneath somebody — exactly what ὑπερφρονήσας in the first sentence described him doing.

sentences.t: Οὕτω τε συνέβη αὐτῷ τῆς ἐξ ἀμφοτέρων διαίτης στερηθῆναι.
sentences.tr: Houtō te synebē autōi tēs ex amphoterōn diaitēs sterēthēnai.
sentences.l: And so it came about for him to be deprived of the life from both.
sentences.i: And so he was cut off from living with either.
sentences.n: συνέβη with the dative and the infinitive, 'it happened to him to…', is this collection's usual way of closing a story on its outcome. στερέομαι takes the genitive of what is lost. τῆς ἐξ ἀμφοτέρων διαίτης is the manner of life he might have had from the one side or the other, and now has from neither.

sentences.t: Οὕτω καὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων οἱ τὰς πατρίδας ἀπολιπόντες καὶ τὰς ἀλλοδαπὰς προκρίνοντες οὔτε ἐν ἐκείναις εὐδοκιμοῦσι διὰ τὸ ξένοι εἶναι καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν πολιτῶν δυσχεραίνονται διὰ τὸ ὑπερπεφρονηκέναι αὐτούς.
sentences.tr: Houtō kai tōn anthrōpōn hoi tas patridas apolipontes kai tas allodapas prokrinontes oute en ekeinais eudokimousi dia to xenoi einai kai hypo tōn politōn dyscherainontai dia to hyperpephronēkenai autous.
sentences.l: So too those among men who have abandoned their own countries and prefer foreign ones do not win esteem in those, on account of being strangers, and are resented by their fellow citizens, on account of having despised them.
sentences.i: So too the men who abandon their own countries and prefer foreign ones: they win no standing abroad, being strangers there, and are resented at home for having looked down on their own people.
sentences.n: The partitive genitive τῶν ἀνθρώπων stands ahead of the article — 'those of men who…' — the standard shape of these morals. οὔτε … καί is a slack correlation where οὔτε … οὔτε is what the balance calls for; Chambry prints the looser pair, and since English has no way to carry a 'neither' that is never answered by a 'nor', the translation simply negates the first limb. διὰ τό with the infinitive gives the cause, twice over; the second, ὑπερπεφρονηκέναι, is a perfect — the contempt is not an act but a thing already on the record. ἀλλοδαπός is 'belonging elsewhere', with γῆ or πόλις understood.
